items.title: Call to Order
notes: Regional Chair K. Redman called the meeting to order at 1:30 p.m. She noted that the purpose of this meeting is to consider a recommendation for the procurement of containerized filtration solutions at the Mannheim water treatment plant.

notes: Regional Chair K. Redman provided a land acknowledgement.

items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
COR-TRY-26-004, Procurement for Pilot- Mannheim Temporary Side Stream Treatment
notes:
Wayne Steffler, Commissioner Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, provided a brief overview of report COR-TRY-26-004. He highlighted that approval to amend the capital budget and approve related procurement actions to advance this time-sensitive project that has been identified as a keystone initiative to address the water supply constraint in the Mannheim Service Area. He confirmed that funding from the province is being sought.

Responding to Council, W. Steffler explained that the procurement process for selecting the proposed vendor H2O Innovation Inc. from a list of seven vendors based on eight distinct criteria. Ayman Khedr, Engineer (Water), further explained that the procurement process went through a detailed process to narrow to the proposed vendor based on specific criteria which was scored with weighted consideration for capacity and expeditious priority. A. Khedr confirmed that the selection criteria included background information of the vendors with reference checks.

Council expressed the importance of confirming funding sources, budget considerations, and communication of implementation and timelines.

A. Shaw confirmed that the funding requested in the staff recommendation is based on the worst-case scenario with added contingencies for unforeseen issues. 

W. Steffler clarified that staff will incorporate water considerations in the 2027 budget and all projects will be evaluated with the lens of expediting future infrastructure projects. W. Steffler confirmed that staff will continue to provide updates on financial implications and the pilot project successes on an ongoing basis with the regular timely updates to Council and the public. He further confirmed that staff will bring a report with the financial strategy for managing the water supply constraint matter.

Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, explained that the in-depth report that Council directed staff to create is still being refined and staff will be receiving input from the development community and once the draft is ready it will be circulated to Regional Council and all Area Municipal Councils.

motions.item_title: COR-TRY-26-004, Procurement for Pilot- Mannheim Temporary Side Stream Treatment
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo amend the capital budget to add a new project; ‘Pilot–Mannheim temporary side stream treatment’, herein called the ‘Mannheim- Containerized Filtration Solution’ in the amount of $15,162,200 to be funded from the Water Capital Reserve Fund, and that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the water capacity shortfall as set out in report COR-TRY-26-004 dated February 6, 2026. Accept the proposal of H2O Innovation Inc. for the Supply of Mannheim Containerized Filtration Solutions in the amount of $7,900,000 plus all applicable taxes. Accept a quote of H2Ontario Inc. for General Contractor and Construction Services for the Containerized Filtration Solutions in the amount of $2,500,000.00 plus all applicable taxes. Plan for additional electrical and engineering work of $4,500,000 plus all applicable taxes; and Authorize the transfer of $15,162,200 (includes taxes) from the Water Capital Reserve to fund the new project.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo amend the capital budget to add a new project; ‘Pilot–Mannheim temporary side stream treatment’, herein called the ‘Mannheim- Containerized Filtration Solution’ in the amount of $15,162,200 to be funded from the Water Capital Reserve Fund, and that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the water capacity shortfall as set out in report COR-TRY-26-004 dated February 6, 2026.

  1. Accept the proposal of H2O Innovation Inc. for the Supply of Mannheim Containerized Filtration Solutions in the amount of $7,900,000 plus all applicable taxes.
  2. Accept a quote of H2Ontario Inc. for General Contractor and Construction Services for the Containerized Filtration Solutions in the amount of $2,500,000.00 plus all applicable taxes.
  3. Plan for additional electrical and engineering work of $4,500,000 plus all applicable taxes; and
  4. Authorize the transfer of $15,162,200 (includes taxes) from the Water Capital Reserve to fund the new project.
